title: EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY’S NOTICE UNDER RULE 17.9.530.11(A) AND VERIFIED PETITION FOR VARIANCE [Petition]

documents.text:
BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION


 IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF EL
 PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR REVISION OF
 ITS RETAIL ELECTRIC RATES,

 EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY,                                        No. 25-00082-UT

        Applicant.



       EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY’S NOTICE UNDER RULE 17.9.530.11(A)
                  AND VERIFIED PETITION FOR VARIANCE

       El Paso Electric Company (“EPE” or “Company”) will be filing an application for revision

of its retail rates in February of 2026. Pursuant to New Mexico Public Regulation Commission

(“NMPRC” or “Commission”) Rule 1.2.2.40 and Rule 17.9.530.11(A) of the New Mexico

Administrative Code (“NMAC”) (“Rule 530”), EPE gives required notice and moves the

Commission to permit a variance of Schedule Q-6 under Rule 530.13(Q)(6) and Rule 530.14(Q)(6)

for EPE’s forthcoming Minimum Data Requirements Filing Package (“Filing Package”) in support

of that application. Specifically, EPE requests a variance to file its audit report prepared under 18

C.F.R. Part 41 for calendar year 2024, which covers part of the Base Period for the Company’s

Filing Package, and to supplement its Filing Package with the 2025 audit report prepared under 18

C.F.R. Part 41, which will cover the remainder of the Base Period, when it becomes available for

filing around mid-April 2026. In support of this Petition, EPE states as follows:

                  LEGAL STANDARD FOR VARIANCE APPLICATION

       1.      Under Rule 17.9.530.11(A) (entitled “Variances”), “an applicant utility unable to

comply fully with any data request contained in Appendix A [of NMPRC Rule 17.9.530 NMAC]

due to good and sufficient cause should give notice in writing to the Commission of the applicant
 utility’s inability to comply with the provisions of such data request at least thirty (30) days prior

to the actual filing of the Minimum Data Requirements Filing Package.”

       2.      The Commission’s Procedural Rules provide that a request for a variance from a

requirement of NMPRC Rule shall: (a) identify the section of the rule from which the variance is

requested; (b) describe the situation that necessitates the variance; (c) describe the effect of

complying with the rule on the applicant if the variance is not granted; (d) describe the result the

variance will have if granted; and (e) describe how the proposed alternative will achieve the

purpose of the rule, and why it is in the public interest. 1.2.2.40(E)(1) – (5) NMAC.

       3.      The Procedural Rules also require a petition for variance to be supported by an

affidavit signed by an officer of the applicant with authority to sign for the applicant. 1.2.2.40(B)

NMAC. This Petition is supported by the Affirmation of Cynthia S. Prieto, EPE’s Vice President

and Controller, which is attached to this Petition as Exhibit 1.

                           CAUSE FOR GRANTING A VARIANCE

  I.   Rule from Which a Variance Is Sought (1.2.2.40.E(1) NMAC)

       4.      Rule 530 defines and specifies the “minimum data requirements to be filed in

support for a tendered new rate schedule or rate schedule which will supersede, supplement, or

otherwise change the provision of a rate schedule required to be on file with this Commission.”

17.9.530.6 NMAC.

       5.      Rule 530 establishes certain data requirements in “Schedule Q” and requires that

the applicant submit its “most current reports as requested herein.” 17.9.530.14(Q) NMAC.

       6.      Appendix A of Rule 530 defines “Schedule Q-6” as comprising the “[o]pinion of

independent public accountants” as follows:

       To satisfy the requirements of this schedule the applicant shall submit a copy of the
       opinion of its independent certified public accountant stating that an independent


                                                  2
        examination of the book amounts and accounting adjustments thereto of the
       applicant utility company's books and records has been made for the Base Period,
       as defined herein, and that the results thereof are in all material respects in
       compliance with the Uniform System of Accounts prescribed by the New Mexico
       Public Service Commission [New Mexico Public Regulation Commission].

17.9.530.14(Q)(6) NMAC.

 II.   Situation that Necessitates the Variance (1.2.2.40.E(2) NMAC)

       7.      EPE is in the process of preparing an application for revision of its retail rates using

a “Base Period,” as defined in Rule 530.7(F), of October 1, 2024 through September 30, 2025, to

establish its “Historical Test Year Period,” as defined in Rule 530.7(S)(2).

       8.      EPE anticipates filing its application in February 2026.

       9.      EPE undergoes an annual audit pursuant to Federal Energy Regulatory Commission

(“FERC”) regulations found at 18 C.F.R. Part 41. EPE must retain the “services of an independent

certified public accountant, or independent licensed public accountant, certified or licensed by a

regulatory authority of a State or other political subdivision of the United States” under 18 C.F.R.

Part 41 to confirm that the Company’s books and records comply “in all material respects” to the

FERC’s “applicable Uniform System of Accounts and published accounting releases.” 18 C.F.R.

§ 41.10(a). The “Uniform System of Accounts” defined in NMPRC Rule 17.3.510.10 adopts by

reference these standards prescribed by FERC. Thus, if the period were the same, the annual audit

would satisfy the requirements of Rule 530.14(Q)(6).

       10.     However, EPE’s audit reports under 18 C.F.R. Part 41 examine the Company’s

records for a calendar year. The most recent available audit report concerns calendar year 2024.

The 2024 report therefore concerns the first three months of the anticipated Base Period, but it

does not cover the whole Base Period. The remainder of the Base Period will be included in the

2025 audit report, which is not yet complete.



                                                  3
        11.     Pursuant to 18 C.F.R. Part 41.11, EPE is required to file its annual audit within 150

days after the close of the fiscal year, or May 31, 2026. Given past experience, EPE anticipates

that the audit report for calendar year 2025 will be available for filing in mid-April 2026.

       12.     EPE may not make its application for new rates under NMPRC Rule 17.1.2.10 after

the calendar year 2025 audit report is complete because the Base Period may not “be more than

one hundred fifty (150) days prior to the date of tender for filing.” 17.9.530.7(F) NMAC. Thus,

EPE must file its application for new rates by the end of February – before the annual audit for

2025 is complete.

III.   Effect of Complying with the Rule (1.2.2.40.E(3) NMAC)

       13.     Preparing a separate audit of the Company’s books and records to comply with Rule

530 Schedule Q-6 for the Base Period would entail a substantial expense that EPE estimates would

be no less than $250,000 and may be as much as $600,000. Such an expense would unnecessarily

duplicate the work EPE must undertake to comply with 18 C.F.R. Part 41.

       14.     Such a result would be inconsistent with the language in Rule 530.14(Q) requiring

an applicant to submit the “most current” reports available. Schedule Q of Rule 530 does not

generally require an applicant utility to commission special audit reports other than those that it

regularly prepares in the normal course of its business.

IV.    Result the Variance Will Have if Granted (1.2.2.40.E(4) NMAC)

       15.     If a variance is granted, EPE will file its 2025 annual audit containing the remaining

nine months of the Base Period (January through September 2025) within five (5) business days

of the date it files with FERC pursuant to 18 C.F.R. Part 41.

       16.     If the Commission grants the requested variance, then EPE will not incur the costs

associated with a separate audit to comply with Rule 530 Schedule Q-6.



                                                 4
        17.     The Commission will have all of the information that Rule 530 Schedule Q-6

requires within months of EPE’s application under NMPRC Rule 17.1.2.10 and before any hearing

on the case is likely to occur.

 V.    Purpose of the Rule and the Public Interest (1.2.2.40.E(5) NMAC)

       18.     The purpose of Rule 530 is to define the minimum data requirements necessary to

evaluate an application under NMPRC Rule 17.1.2.10. See 17.9.530.6 NMAC. The requested

variance is consistent with that purpose because the Company will provide the information

responsive to Schedule Q-6 that is available at the time of filing and will supplement to provide

the remaining information well before any hearing or decision on the application.

       19.     The requested variance is consistent with the public interest because it prevents the

Company from incurring unnecessary and duplicative costs that may ultimately affect the costs

borne by ratepayers. EPE will perform the required audits in accordance with 18 C.F.R. Part 41

and should not be required to incur duplicative costs under Rule 530 merely because the 2025 audit

will not be available for filing until April 2026.

                                          CONCLUSION

       EPE respectfully requests that the Commission grant it a variance from NMPRC Rule

17.9.530.13(Q)(6) and NMPRC Rule 17.9.530.14(Q)(6) for its forthcoming Filing Package in

support of an application for a new rate schedule under NMPRC Rule 17.1.2.10 anticipated in

February 2026. The variance will permit EPE to submit its 2024 audit report under 18 C.F.R. §

41.10(a) with its initial filing on the condition that EPE supplement the Filing Package with the

2025 audit report when it becomes available.

       Pursuant to NMPRC Rule 17.9.530.11(B), EPE requests that the Commission render its

decision within fifteen days of this Petition for Variance.



                                                     5
        Staff does not oppose this Petition for Variance with the understanding that the audited

numbers do not change the February filing.
